case_summary: A transport logger must resume sampling after power loss and ensure exports do not omit readings represented as recorded on its display.
answer: The current loop cannot guarantee this: `display(sample)` precedes a buffered append, and `flush()` has no documented power-loss durability or atomicity. Define “recorded” as a durable media acknowledgement; show a sample as pending until then, and report save failure distinctly. Keep one sampling/write owner: append a framed record containing a monotonic sequence number, sample and checksum, then use a storage operation whose contract guarantees persistence across power loss before marking it recorded. On boot/export, scan and validate records, tolerate or discard only a torn final frame, detect sequence gaps, and refuse or clearly flag incomplete exports; never silently copy an unchecked file. This requires a card/API (or added power protection) that actually provides the needed durability. Framing detects torn records but cannot repair arbitrary card corruption or make an undocumented flush durable. If hardware cannot provide that contract, the requested guarantee is impossible; display “sampled” separately from “saved” and expose uncertainty. The smallest alternative—flush each line and keep verbatim export—costs less but cannot establish the guarantee. Synchronous durable writes may delay or stop one-second sampling, while the device has no backup memory. Product must choose the acceptable delay and whether sampling continues after save failure. Verify on target hardware with cuts around writes/acknowledgements and reboot recovery; assert every displayed-saved sequence appears in export or export explicitly fails. Also exercise torn tail, missing sequence, full and removed card. No implementation or power-cut behavior was verified here.
